newsitem.title: USA: US House Panel caps FY98 EEP funding at $270 mln.
newsitem.headline: US House Panel caps FY98 EEP funding at $270 mln.

text.p: The House Appropriations subcommittee on agriculture Wednesday approved a fiscal 1998 spending plan that limits funding for the Export Enhancement Program to $270 million, well below the Clinton administration's request of $500 million.
Committee Chairman Joe Skeen, a New Mexico Republican, said the EEP spending cap was needed to provide full funding for the federal crop insurance program.
The spending bill will go next to the full House Appropriations Committee, where it could be changed.
Congress initially funded EEP at $100 million in fiscal 1997 but later cut that to $10 million to help provide disaster assistance for Northern states flood victims.

USDA has not subsidized wheat and other agricultural exports under EEP for nearly two years. However, with lower prices currently there has been some speculation that USDA might revive the program sometime in the 1997/98 wheat marketing year.
"We did not ask them," a subcommittee aide told reporters when asked if USDA now thought $270 million would be adequate for EEP in fiscal 1998.
Given current wheat stock levels and prices, "they really have no intention of using it (EEP)," the aide said referring to USDA. "Everyone in town knows it."
The fiscal 1998 spending bill is scheduled to go to the full appropriations committee on July 9.
